spec.doc: Runs atomically at deploy time, so nobody can front-run initialization. `protocol_fee_share_bps` is the default protocol/LP split for new markets; 10_000 keeps the whole fee with the protocol (pre-upgrade behaviour). Pass 0 to give all fees to the market creators.

spec.name: buy

spec.doc: Categorical-market counterpart of `buy`: spend `collateral_in` on `outcome_index` shares. Returns shares received; reverts if fewer than `min_shares_out` would be received. No v2 (deadline/limit) variant yet — see the categorical notes in `docs/architecture.md`.

The average price includes the fee (`fee` is part of `collateral_in`) and, for a NO buy, is compared against the NO price. Because the deadline check runs before `require_auth`, an expired transaction fails cheaply. A limit above BPS can never pass for a buy and is rejected as invalid.
spec.name: buy_v2

spec.doc: The creator (the LP) claims their share of accrued trade fees at any time, including before finality. Returns the amount claimed (0 when nothing is pending, mirroring `sweep_fees`). Works for both market kinds (the fee side-entries are keyed by the shared market id).

spec.name: claim_pool_remainders

spec.doc: Creates a categorical market with 2..=8 outcomes and seeds the pool. `creator` becomes the sole LP and receives the leftover shares of the likelier outcomes. `probs_bps` must have one entry per outcome with every probability in `math::MIN_PROB_BPS..=math::MAX_PROB_BPS` and the entries summing to exactly BPS. Collateral, id space, pause switch, fee snapshot and `resolution_hash` commitment are shared with `create_market`; the pool is the same FPMM with the reserve-product invariant generalised to n outcomes (see `math_categorical`). Per-market circuit breakers are price-based and binary-only, so categorical markets are not snapshotted with them — nor with a `FeeSchedule`: they always charge their flat `fee_bps`.
spec.name: create_categorical_market

spec.doc: Creates a market and seeds the pool. `creator` becomes the sole LP. `initial_yes_bps` in [100, 9900] sets the opening YES probability; the creator receives the leftover shares of the likelier outcome. When a default dynamic fee schedule is set it is snapshotted for this market (see `set_default_fee_schedule`); otherwise the market charges the flat `DefaultFeeBps`.
spec.name: create_market

spec.doc: `create_market` with an explicit per-market `FeeSchedule`. Validated against `MAX_FEE_BPS` and the current default schedule's `max_bps` (creators can undercut protocol policy, never exceed it), then snapshotted for this market's lifetime.

spec.doc: Permissionless close-out of a final market after its redemption deadline. Sweeps the market's entire remaining balance — value reserved for shares never redeemed, an unclaimed LP remainder, per-holder rounding dust and accrued fees — to the treasury, and marks the market closed so nothing can ever pay out again. The deadline is `redeem_deadline(market_id)` = `finalized_at + horizon_secs`, the horizon being snapshotted at creation from the admin default. Anyone who redeems before the deadline is paid the exact `settle_value` they would have received without this call; only shares still unredeemed at the deadline are forfeit, and their value goes to the treasury rather than the LP so the LP cannot profit from suppressing redemptions. Returns the amount swept. The swept total is exactly the market's contract balance: sets plus fees minus everything already paid out.

spec.doc: Per-market TWAP accumulator (issue #11). Lives in its own entry so the `Market` XDR stays unchanged. Semantics: at the start of every trade the price that held since the last trade is folded into `price_cumulative` over the elapsed interval; the post-trade price then becomes `last_price_bps` until the next trade. That is the Uniswap-v2 model, and it is what makes manipulation expensive — moving the average requires holding the price away from fair value across one or more ledger boundaries, not just within a single transaction. Overflow analysis: `last_price_bps <= 10_000` and each interval adds `price * dt` seconds. A 100-year market lifetime accumulates at most `10_000 * 3.2e9 ~ 3.2e13`; even a pathological `dt = u64::MAX` gives `1.8e19 * 1e4 = 1.8e23`. `i128::MAX` is ~1.7e38, so there is no feasible lifetime that overflows — and every step is `checked_*` anyway, so a violation rejects the transaction instead of corrupting the accumulator.

spec.doc: V3 commitment envelope. Commitment domain: `sha256("oracledesk:resolution-spec-v3" || XDR(ResolutionSpecV3))`. The domain prefix differs from V2 (`"oracledesk:resolution-spec"`) so a V3 preimage with `invalid_threshold = 0` cannot collide with the corresponding V2 hash. Fields `version`, `network_id`, `market_core`, `salt` and `rule` carry identical semantics to [`ResolutionSpecV2`]. The additions are the two Invalid-policy fields below.

fields.doc: Only meaningful when `invalid_threshold > 0`; must be `false` otherwise. When `false`, an Invalid quorum can never displace a pending Yes/No proposal. When `true`, at most one displacement is permitted per market (tracked by `DataKey::InvalidDisplaced`).
fields.name: invalid_allow_displacement

fields.doc: Minimum Invalid-attestation count (address count, committee members, or weight threshold) for an Invalid quorum. `0` means no Invalid policy: legacy V2 semantics, where Invalid uses the Yes/No threshold and displacement is unrestricted. A real policy threshold is always at least 1, so `0` is an unambiguous sentinel. When non-zero it must be strictly greater than the Yes/No threshold of `rule` and at most the member count (enforced by `validate_invalid_policy`). Price / WeightedKeys rules reject a non-zero value (`InvalidConfig`).
fields.name: invalid_threshold

fields.doc: `sha256(network passphrase)`, i.e. `env.ledger().network_id()`.
fields.name: network_id

fields.doc: Must be 3; `register_spec_v3` rejects any other value.
fields.name: version

spec.name: ResolutionSpecV3

spec.doc: Display metadata of a scalar market: the `[lower, upper]` range of the committed resolution spec, in the feed's raw units. Stored under `DataKey::Scalar(u64)` at creation; the resolver's revealed spec is the authoritative copy, this entry only tells UIs what to display.
spec.name: ScalarMeta

spec.doc: Scalar (range) counterpart of [`PriceConfig`]. The market settles on the fractional position of `price` inside `[lower, upper]`: `payout_long_bps = (clamped_price - lower) / (upper - lower)`, and the SHORT side pays the complement. A reading below the range clamps to `lower` (LONG pays 0), above to `upper` (LONG pays 1.0); a non-positive reading is an invalid price, never a clamp.

fields.doc: Bottom of the staked range. Validated `0 <= lower < upper`, with `upper` capped so `upper * BPS` cannot overflow.
fields.name: lower

spec.name: ScalarPriceConfig

spec.doc: Per-market settlement bookkeeping (issue #14). Lives in its own entry so the `Market` XDR stays unchanged.

fields.doc: `finalize_market` has swept the market's remaining balance; no redemption or claim can ever pay out again.
fields.name: closed

fields.doc: Timestamp of `resolve` / `void_market`; 0 while the market is Open.
fields.name: finalized_at

fields.doc: Redemption window, snapshotted at creation from the admin default. `redeem_deadline = finalized_at + horizon_secs`.
fields.name: horizon_secs

fields.doc: Outcome shares held outside the pool (user positions), still redeemable. `redeem` decrements the redeeming holder's shares on both sides, so a losing-side redemption (payout 0) still clears here.
fields.name: outstanding_yes

fields.doc: Share/pool collateral already paid to holders and the LP (`redeem` payouts + the pool value of `claim_pool_remainder`); tracks what of `sets_minted` has left the market. LP fees paid alongside the pool remainder are **not** counted here: they never entered `sets_minted` (issue #276, see docs/formal-verification.md "Settlement").
fields.name: paid_out

spec.name: SettleState

spec.doc: Why a market in a batch call did not settle. `Duplicate` is reserved: ids are validated strictly ascending first, so a duplicate is rejected as `InvalidAmount` before the batch runs and never reaches a skip.
spec.name: SkipReason

fields.doc: Raw Ed25519 public key. For a `G...` account address this is `StrKey.decodeEd25519PublicKey(address)`; `C...` addresses have none.
fields.name: pubkey

fields.doc: Total weight that must sign one outcome. Choose it above half the total weight so two outcomes can never both reach it.
fields.name: weight_threshold

cases.doc: A batch call carried no ids or more than `MAX_BATCH` of them.
cases.name: BatchTooLarge

cases.doc: `create_market` used a token missing from, or disabled in, the admin collateral allow-list (#151).
cases.name: CollateralNotAllowed

cases.doc: Inbound collateral transfer delivered fewer (or different) units than expected, e.g. a fee-on-transfer or under-delivering token (#137).
cases.name: CollateralShortfall

cases.doc: Allow-list parameters failed validation (decimals, seed bounds).
cases.name: InvalidCollateralParams

cases.doc: `outcome_index` is not a valid outcome of this categorical market.
cases.name: InvalidOutcomeIndex

cases.doc: `buy_v2` / `sell_v2` average execution price worse than the limit.
cases.name: LimitPriceExceeded

cases.doc: The market was closed out and its remaining value swept.
cases.name: MarketClosedOut

cases.doc: Legacy market created before `SettleState` existed: outstanding shares cannot be reconstructed on-chain, so it has no deadline and cannot be finalized (still fully redeemable).
cases.name: NotSupported

cases.doc: `observe` / `twap` asked for a time older than every surviving observation of the market (the ring keeps the most recent 16).
cases.name: ObservationTooOld

cases.doc: A proposed admin handover was not accepted within its `expires_at`.
cases.name: PendingAdminExpired

cases.doc: A single trade would move the price more than `max_impact_bps`. (Both this and the band reject the whole invocation, so their events, if any, roll back with it — see the note on `BreakerConfig`.)
cases.name: PriceImpactTooHigh

cases.doc: Market already closed by `finalize_market`; redemption is over.
cases.name: RedemptionClosed

params.doc: Requested opening probabilities, one per outcome, summing to BPS.
params.name: probs_bps

params.doc: None means the market was voided.
params.name: outcome_index

spec.doc: V1 event: default fee for new markets changed.
spec.name: DefaultFeeSet

spec.doc: Same sweep as `FeesSwept` plus the actual recipient. New event rather than new fields so the existing `FeesSwept` XDR stays stable for indexers; both are emitted on every sweep.
spec.name: FeesSweptTo

params.doc: Everything swept to the treasury: expired user claims, an unclaimed LP remainder, rounding dust and accrued fees.
params.name: swept

params.doc: The part of `swept` that was reserved for shares never redeemed.
params.name: unclaimed_user

params.doc: Rounding left over after per-holder void floors were accounted for.
params.name: dust

params.doc: None means the market was voided.
params.name: outcome

params.doc: LONG payout per complete set, 0..=BPS; the SHORT leg pays the complement. `MarketResolved` is never emitted for scalar markets.
params.name: payout_long_bps

spec.doc: V1 event: market pause state changed.
spec.name: PausedSet

params.doc: Pool remainder plus any LP fees drained in the same call.
params.name: payout

spec.doc: V1 event: pool remainder claimed by creator after market finality.
spec.name: PoolRemainderClaimedV1

spec.doc: Positions moved between holders. Indexers that track balances from `Trade`/`Redeemed` must also apply this event (see docs/architecture.md).
spec.name: PositionTransferred

spec.doc: Same trade as `Trade` plus the realised fee rate. New event rather than a new field so the existing `Trade` XDR stays stable for indexers (the `FeesSweptTo` convention); both are emitted on every binary trade. `fee_bps` is the effective dynamic rate applied, already snapshotted into `fee` — indexers can recover it from `fee / collateral` but not exactly, because `fee` carries the ceiling rounding.
spec.name: TradeV2
